table.name: sale_record_events
columns: sale_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sales(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT

identity.id_formula: crypto.randomUUID() generated before the atomic batch and enforced as a lowercase RFC 4122 version-4 UUID by SQL; id is an opaque row identifier, while the composite unique key is the retry identity
identity.rule: kind is payload under the unique act identity and cannot create a second record for one act. Do not concatenate unescaped tuple parts into id.

checks: source_kind is one of sale_status, sale_customer, sale_settlement, sale_bulk_status, sale_bulk_update, return_create, return_edit, return_bulk
generation is an integer from 0 through 1000000
kind is one of the frozen F74 kinds except legacy_sale_change, which is synthesized only from legacy rows and is never appended to this table
via is apply, undo, or redo
actor_username is null or at most 120 characters
subject is null or at most 240 characters
occurred_at is non-empty and at most 40 characters
changes_json is a valid JSON array with 1..12 elements and at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes; the migration measures bytes with length(CAST(changes_json AS BLOB))
request_digest is null or a 64-character lowercase SHA-256 hex string
response_json is null or a valid JSON object no larger than 65536 UTF-8 bytes, measured with length(CAST(response_json AS BLOB))

source_kind and kind are an allowed writer pair, and generation/via are coupled: generation zero is apply; only replay-capable receipt sources permit later generations, with odd generations undo and even generations redo
index: UNIQUE(source_kind,source_id,generation) WHERE source_kind IN ('sale_status','sale_customer','return_edit') prevents one direct request identity from targeting two sales

return_edit_receipt_table.name: return_mutation_receipts
return_edit_receipt_table.purpose: Actor-scoped exact retry for customer-return edits, including valid edits that do not change the parent sale status and therefore must not invent a Sales Records event.
columns: return_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES returns(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
sale_id INTEGER REFERENCES sales(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT
identity_and_indexes: id is crypto.randomUUID() generated before the atomic edit batch and SQL-enforced as a lowercase RFC 4122 version-4 UUID
UNIQUE(actor_id,mutation_kind,request_id) prevents concurrent duplicate execution and cross-return reuse for one actor
INDEX(return_id,occurred_at,id) supports exact retry/diagnostic lookup without scanning
sql_checks: actor_id and return_id are positive SQLite integers; sale_id is null or a positive SQLite integer
request_id is trimmed non-empty text of at most 120 UTF-8 bytes
request_digest is exactly 64 lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal characters
request_json is a valid JSON object at most 131072 UTF-8 bytes measured by length(CAST(request_json AS BLOB))

response_json is a valid JSON object at most 65536 UTF-8 bytes measured by length(CAST(response_json AS BLOB)); it has exactly positive integer id and non-empty updated_at text of at most 40 UTF-8 bytes
occurred_at is non-empty text of at most 40 characters
return_edit_receipt_table.immutability: BEFORE UPDATE always aborts. BEFORE DELETE aborts unless maintenance mode is restore or sale_record_events_reset_guard contains mode reset and a non-empty token. No ordinary retention/pruning path may update or delete receipts.
server_validation: Require client_request_id matching the existing bounded client-id normalizer and expected_updated_at for every PATCH /returns/:id edit before any write.

Build a normalized canonical request with return_id, expected_updated_at, items in submitted order, reason/return_type/notes presence and values, server-derived refund line inputs, and branch presence/value. Preserve meaningful missing versus null with explicit presence booleans.

Hash the canonical JSON with SHA-256. Lookup by actor_id, mutation_kind edit, and request_id before the stale revision check; exact digest returns the stored response, while any digest or target mismatch returns 409 idempotency_conflict.
Allow response_json only as exactly {id: positive integer, updated_at: bounded non-empty text}; do not retain contact data, arbitrary errors, nested values, or the response body beyond these scalars.
atomic_handler_order: Read the return and parent sale, capture return_write_revision, sale_write_revision, exact parent status, and normalized request before any write.
Compute the projected parent status from other active customer returns plus the proposed item set, using sale_item_id first and product fallback allocation without double-counting duplicate products.
Put return revision guard and sale revision/current-status guard first in the existing compensated edit batch.

Put the return row/item rewrite and every return_item_batch_allocations insert in that same batch; identify each just-inserted return item by the newest id for that return before any allocation insert changes last_insert_rowid().
Put the guarded parent sales update next only when its status changes, followed by the conditional immutable return_edit event whose before/after matches the guarded snapshot.
Insert return_mutation_receipts last in the same batch, with its UUID also used as the conditional event source_id, so no receipt can exist without every essential edit effect.

After a successful batch, only operational audit/cache/broadcast work may remain. On any batch failure, SQLite rolls back return, allocations, parent status, event, and receipt together; the existing catch compensates only pre-batch lot/damaged writes. Remove the old post-batch allocation and sale-status writes.
return_edit_receipt_table.conditional_event: Emit one return_edit/status_changed event only when the guarded parent sale status changes. Generation is 0, via apply, source_id is return_mutation_receipts.id, subject is the historical return number, actor/time are captured, and the one sale_status change is exact known_value before/after. If status is unchanged or the return has no parent sale, persist the receipt but emit no event.
lifecycle: BACKUP_TABLES: insert return_mutation_receipts after returns and before sale_record_events, preserving parent-first restore order; include it in SALE_REPLAY_RESTORE_BUNDLE so every scoped sales/returns/events backup widens to include it.

Reverse restore deletion deletes sale_record_events before return_mutation_receipts before returns/sales. Restore insertion restores returns/sales before return_mutation_receipts before sale_record_events.

FACTORY_RESET_TABLES and reset-data products+includeSales, sales, and all scopes delete sale_record_events first, then return_mutation_receipts, then return/items/sales, under the same fresh atomic reset guard token.
Backup dependency validation must require returns and sales when a receipt is present, and generated scoped/full FK-on backup restore tests must include one receipt with and without a linked sale.
Ordinary audit retention, action-history retention, and any 21-day pruning exclude return_mutation_receipts.

rules: Reject unknown source_kind, kind, via, field, or field-for-kind combinations.
Require each change to contain exactly field, before, and after.
Require each side to be exactly known_value with value, known_none without value, or unknown without value.
Reject duplicate fields and equal before/after states.

Validate nested customer, membership, driver, item, item-list, payment, and payment-details shapes and scalar bounds. New customer values permit only stable id and display name; phone and address are forbidden. Existing undo receipts may retain their pre-existing private fields internally, but projection into changes_json removes them.

When response_json is used for direct-request idempotency, permit only the endpoint's fixed success/id/status/timestamp response keys and their exact scalar types. Never persist a request body, contact details, nested objects, arrays, or arbitrary error payload in response_json.
Require the complete serialized @events array to be at most 131072 UTF-8 bytes.
Serialize only the validated normalized structure; never serialize request bodies or arbitrary audit variables.
server_validation_before_sql.batch_insert: One INSERT...SELECT FROM json_each(@events) statement writes all changed members. A 25-member bulk action or replay therefore adds exactly one D1 batch statement, not 25. saleBulkStatus, saleBulkUpdate, and returnBulkAction each change their bounded helper to receive eventsBytes and require eventsBytes <= 131072, snapshotBytes + eventsBytes <= 512000, and the final statement count <= 500 after the event statement is added.

writer_matrix.idempotency: Require a stable client_request_id for every non-noop status request. The canonical digest includes the target sale id plus status, notes, cancellation, settlement, expected revision, and other accepted semantic fields. Save SHA-256 digest and response_json in the event. An exact retry returns response_json; reuse with another digest or sale id is 409. Event and sale/audit/stock writes share one guarded batch.

Require a stable client_request_id. The canonical digest includes the target sale id, target customer id, and expected revision. Save canonical digest and response. Exact retry returns the saved response; conflicting reuse or sale id is 409. F72's active UI continues to use sale_bulk_update.

writer_matrix.writer: sale settlement/payment correction Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for each guarded replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor-scoped request receipt and generation guard are stable before the batch. Append event in the same batch as receipt creation or generation increment.

writer_matrix.writer: sale bulk status Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor/request receipt and generation guard. One validated json_each event insert covers up to 25 changed sale members atomically.

writer_matrix.writer: sale bulk customer/payment/driver Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor/request receipt and generation guard. One validated json_each event insert covers up to 25 changed sale members atomically.

The return's required client_request_id resolves to one durable returns.id before retry. Append the sale-status event in the same guarded batch as the status update; an existing return retry creates no second event. Supplier returns emit no sale event.

Require a stable client_request_id and expected_updated_at for edits. Lookup the actor-scoped return_mutation_receipts row before stale checking. The normalized canonical digest includes the target return id, expected timestamp, ordered item inputs, and every accepted reason/type/notes/refund/branch semantic field with meaningful missing/null presence. Exact retry returns the fixed stored response; conflicting reuse or another target is 409. The return and sale revision/current-status guards, complete return rewrite and allocations, conditional event, and receipt commit in one batch. Supplier returns remain refused by this route.

writer_matrix.writer: return bulk status Apply, Undo, Redo
writer_matrix.generation: 0 for Apply; old generation + 1 for replay
writer_matrix.idempotency: Existing actor/request receipt and generation guard. Compute one before/after sale status per distinct affected sale after the return statements and insert all events with one validated json_each statement. Supplier returns and non-status bulk fields emit no sale event.

legacy_cutover.detail: Load durable events first. Every post-cutover writer stamps its existing audit/action-history twin with the same source_kind, source_id, generation, and sale_id; existing receipt rows already expose that identity. Suppress a legacy candidate only when both it and an event expose an exact four-key match. Keep every old row with no exact tuple, including unknown legacy_sale_change.
legacy_cutover.count: Count sale_record_events directly. Each legacy receipt family contributes max(0, 1 + generation - exact matching event count for that source_kind/source_id/sale_id and generation range). Audit/return candidates use NOT EXISTS on the same four-key identity. No actor, state, status, or timestamp proximity matching.
legacy_cutover.parity: The detail and count paths share the same source-kind mapping and four-key anti-join test in focused SQLite fixtures.

immutability_and_lifecycle.trigger: sale_record_events and return_mutation_receipts each have a BEFORE UPDATE trigger that always aborts. Each BEFORE DELETE aborts unless either the existing system_flags key maintenance has JSON mode restore, or the dedicated system_flags key sale_record_events_reset_guard has JSON mode reset and a non-empty token. Restore only needs DELETE plus INSERT, so it never weakens either UPDATE guard.
immutability_and_lifecycle.reset_sequence: Each reset uses one D1 batch whose first statement inserts sale_record_events_reset_guard with mode reset and a fresh non-empty token, whose next applicable statement deletes sale_record_events before sales, whose existing statements preserve child-first order, and whose last statement token-guards deletion of sale_record_events_reset_guard. A failed D1 batch rolls back the guard and every delete. The ordinary maintenance parser remains restore-only; the reset guard is internal and cannot outlive or expose a partially completed atomic batch.
backup: Add return_mutation_receipts after returns and before sale_record_events in BACKUP_TABLES, so restore inserts its sale/return parents first and reverse-deletes the event child then the receipt.
Add return_mutation_receipts and sale_record_events to SALE_REPLAY_RESTORE_BUNDLE so scoped restore cannot split events from sales/returns/receipts.
The existing maintenance mode restore bypass permits reverse-order child deletion; event UPDATE remains forbidden.
immutability_and_lifecycle.factory_reset: Add sale_record_events then return_mutation_receipts before returns/sales in FACTORY_RESET_TABLES and wrap that existing atomic batch with the dedicated reset guard statements.
immutability_and_lifecycle.reset_data: Add sale_record_events then return_mutation_receipts before returns/sales in products+includeSales, sales, and all delete lists; wrap each existing atomic delete batch with the dedicated reset guard statements. The delete scope remains child-first and narrow. createSectionBackup automatically widens any section touching a sales/replay table to the complete SALE_REPLAY_RESTORE_BUNDLE in BACKUP_TABLES parent-first order, so the mandatory recovery artifact passes the same dependency preflight used by restore.
immutability_and_lifecycle.retention: No ephemeral-retention path references sale_record_events or return_mutation_receipts. Ordinary 21-day audit and action-history pruning cannot erase either table.

permissions_and_audit.permissions: No new mutation route. Each append runs only inside its existing authorized writer/replay path after that path's permission check.
permissions_and_audit.audit: Existing audit logs remain. Record events add immutable display provenance and do not replace security/audit logging.

frontend_prerequisites: The ordinary sale-status caller must create one client_request_id when the user begins an action, persist it through unknown responses, and replace it only after a terminal success or a deliberate new action.

The legacy direct-customer caller, if retained, and customer-return edit caller must follow the same stable client_request_id lifecycle. Return edit must continue sending expected_updated_at. Older queued edits with no persisted id are quarantined as refresh_required without mutation; the server never invents an id after an unknown outcome.
Do not enable a backend requirement until these callers and focused unknown-response retry tests are integrated in the same release candidate.
required_tests: Native SQLite Apply/Undo/Redo for settlement, sale bulk status, sale bulk update, and return bulk status.
Native SQLite create/edit customer return sale-status before/after and supplier non-event.
Stable retry returns prior response; conflicting request-id reuse fails; concurrent revision loses atomically.
Maximum 25-member bulk fixtures prove exactly one added statement and remain below existing 500/512000 bounds.

Malformed kind/field/state/nested value, legacy_sale_change insertion, 13 changes, per-event oversized JSON, aggregate events JSON over 131072 bytes, combined snapshot plus events over 512000 bytes, duplicate field, and equal-state events fail before SQL.
One direct client_request_id cannot target two sales or returns, even concurrently; each canonical digest includes its route target id.
Migration CHECKs, append-only triggers, reset maintenance order, backup/restore dependency coverage, factory reset, sales reset, all reset, products includeSales.
Audit pruning leaves every new event and exact legacy fallback; count equals detail for mixed pre/post migration history.
